content: 1. Ethosuximide's metabolism is influenced by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Exercise caution and monitor closely when co-administered. 2. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of ethotoin by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 3. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of etoposide by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of etrasimod through mechanisms other than CYP enzymes. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Increased exposure to etrasimod is expected in CYP2C9 poor metabolizers when co-administered with moderate to strong CYP2C8 inhibitors. 6. Efavirenz decreases the levels of etravirine by increasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 7. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of etravirine by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism but decreases its levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use an alternative drug. 8. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of efavirenz by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 9. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of eucalyptus by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 10. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of everolimus by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 11. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of exemestane by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. For patients on exemestane with a potent CYP3A4 inducer, the recommended dose is 50 mg daily after a meal. 12. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of fedratinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. The effect of co-administering a strong CYP3A4 inducer with fedratinib has not been studied. 14. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of felbamate by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of felodipine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of fentanyl by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inducers may reduce fentanyl plasma concentrations, leading to reduced efficacy or withdrawal symptoms in dependent patients. Both drugs increase sedation. 17. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of fentanyl intranasal by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inducers may reduce fentanyl plasma concentrations, leading to reduced efficacy or withdrawal symptoms in dependent patients. Both drugs increase sedation. 18. Efavirenz and fentanyl iontophoretic transdermal system both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of fentanyl transdermal by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inducers may reduce fentanyl plasma concentrations, leading to reduced efficacy or withdrawal symptoms in dependent patients. Both drugs increase sedation. 20. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of fentanyl transmucosal by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inducers may reduce fentanyl plasma concentrations, leading to reduced efficacy or withdrawal symptoms in dependent patients. Both drugs increase sedation. 21. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of fesoterodine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of fexinidazole by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, potentially increasing the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. 23. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of finasteride by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 24. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of finerenone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Efavirenz and fingolimod both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Efavirenz and flecainide both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of flibanserin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Strong CYP3A4 inducers significantly reduce flibanserin systemic exposure. 28. Efavirenz and fluconazole both increase the QTc interval. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 29. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of fludrocortisone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Fludrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of efavirenz by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 30. Efavirenz and fluoxetine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Efavirenz and fluphenazine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of flurazepam by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of flurbiprofen by altering CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of fluvastatin by altering CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Fluvoxamine increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by altering CYP2B6 metabolism. Efavirenz and fluvoxamine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Efavirenz and formoterol both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Fosamprenavir and efavirenz both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. 38. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 39. Efavirenz and foscarnet both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 40. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of fosphenytoin by altering CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of efavirenz by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 41. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of fostamatinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of fostemsavir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 43. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of fruquintinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 44. Efavirenz and ganaxolone both increase sedation. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of ganaxolone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 45. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of gefitinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 46. Efavirenz and gemifloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Efavirenz and gemtuzumab both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 48. Efavirenz and gilteritinib both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Efavirenz and givinostat both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 50. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of glasdegib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 51. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 52. Efavirenz and goserelin both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Efavirenz and granisetron both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 55. Griseofulvin decreases the levels or effects of efavirenz by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 56. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of guanfacine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 57. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of haloperidol by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Efavirenz and haloperidol both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Efavirenz and histrelin both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of hydrocodone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 60. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of hydrocortisone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Hydrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of efavirenz by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 61. Efavirenz and hydroxychloroquine sulfate both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 62. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of hydroxyprogesterone caproate by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Efavirenz and hydroxyzine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 64. Efavirenz decreases the levels of ibrutinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 65. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of ibuprofen by altering CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
